detail.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Fixes a resume bug in `OptimizerParamScheduler.load_state_dict`. The method called `self.step(increment=num_steps)` before it restored `start_wd`, `end_wd`, `wd_incr_steps` and `wd_incr_style` from the checkpoint. `step()` writes both `lr` and `weight_decay` into every param group, so right after a resume the param groups held the learning rate from the checkpoint schedule but the weight decay from the constructor arguments. The scheduler object itself ended up with the right values, only the param groups were stale.

This matters because `train_step` in `megatron/training/training.py` calls `optimizer.step()` before `opt_param_scheduler.step()`, so the first optimizer step after a resume ran with the wrong weight decay. Every later step is fine because the next scheduler step rewrites the param groups. The bug only shows up when `--use-checkpoint-opt_param-scheduler` is set and the weight decay arguments differ from the ones stored in the checkpoint. With matching arguments the two schedules agree and nothing is visible.

The fix moves the `num_iters` / `num_steps` lookup and the `step()` call to the end of `load_state_dict`, after every value has been restored. Legacy checkpoints that only carry the old learning rate keys still load the same way. No other behaviour changes.

The change touches two files.

- `megatron/core/optimizer_param_scheduler.py` moves the `step()` call to the end of `load_state_dict`, adds a two line comment saying why, and adds the blank line after the module docstring that black 26.3.0 requires. That blank line is the only formatting change. black already fails on this file on main without it, so the formatter run for this PR could not pass otherwise.
- `tests/unit_tests/test_optimizer_param_scheduler.py` adds `test_load_state_dict_applies_checkpoint_weight_decay`. It loads a checkpoint whose weight decay schedule differs from the constructor and checks that the param group holds the checkpoint value and that lr and weight decay agree with the scheduler. On main the param group holds 0.05 while the scheduler reports 0.2, so the test fails there.

## Tests

Run on a CPU GitHub Actions runner with torch 2.14.0+cpu and Python 3.12.

- With this branch, all 19 tests in `tests/unit_tests/test_optimizer_param_scheduler.py` pass and black, isort and ruff are clean on both changed files: https://github.com/Nicholas022400701/oss-ci/actions/runs/35307716702
- Same test file on main plus only the new test. The new test fails with `assert 0.05 == 0.2`: https://github.com/Nicholas022400701/oss-ci/actions/runs/35306817760

## Issue tracking

Linked issue: none. I searched the issues and pull requests for this method and did not find a report. #4705 is about matching param groups on load and does not touch this ordering.

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` ([guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/docs/developer/determinism/testing.md))
- [ ] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation
- [x] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR

Notes on the boxes. No functional test because the change is covered by the unit test. No kernel is touched. The method keeps its existing type hints and no documentation describes this ordering. `tools/autoformat.sh` needs a remote and pylint, so I ran the same black, isort and ruff commands on the two changed files in the CI run linked above instead.

AI disclosure: I used an AI coding agent to help write this patch, the test and this description. I have read every line of the change myself and I will answer review comments personally.

The three commits are signed off. I can squash them into one if you prefer.

detail.title: Fix stale weight decay after OptimizerParamScheduler.load_state_dict

files.patch:
@@ -1,6 +1,7 @@
 # Copyright (c) 2022, NVIDIA CORPORATION. All rights reserved.
 
 """Learning rate decay and weight decay incr functions."""
+
 import logging
 import math
 from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Optional, TypedDict
@@ -383,12 +384,6 @@ def load_state_dict(self, state_dict: dict) -> None:
             self.lr_decay_style, lr_decay_style_, 'learning rate decay style'
         )
 
-        if 'num_iters' in state_dict:
-            num_steps = state_dict['num_iters']
-        else:
-            num_steps = state_dict['num_steps']
-        self.step(increment=num_steps)
-
         if 'start_wd' in state_dict:
             self.start_wd = self._check_and_set(
                 self.start_wd, state_dict['start_wd'], "start weight decay"
@@ -402,3 +397,11 @@ def load_state_dict(self, state_dict: dict) -> None:
             self.wd_incr_style = self._check_and_set(
                 self.wd_incr_style, state_dict['wd_incr_style'], "weight decay incr style"
             )
+
+        if 'num_iters' in state_dict:
+            num_steps = state_dict['num_iters']
+        else:
+            num_steps = state_dict['num_steps']
+        # Write the loaded schedule into the param groups only after every value above has
+        # been restored, so lr and weight_decay both follow the checkpoint from the first step.
+        self.step(increment=num_steps)

@@ -299,6 +299,51 @@ def test_load_state_dict(mock_optimizer):
     assert scheduler.wd_incr_style == 'cosine'
 
 
+def test_load_state_dict_applies_checkpoint_weight_decay(mock_optimizer):
+    """The param groups must follow the checkpoint weight decay schedule right after loading.
+
+    load_state_dict used to call step() before it restored the weight decay values, so the
+    weight_decay written into the param groups came from the constructor arguments while the
+    lr already came from the checkpoint. The first optimizer step after a resume then ran with
+    the wrong weight decay.
+    """
+    scheduler = OptimizerParamScheduler(
+        optimizer=mock_optimizer,
+        init_lr=0.01,
+        max_lr=0.1,
+        min_lr=0.001,
+        lr_warmup_steps=100,
+        lr_decay_steps=1000,
+        lr_decay_style='linear',
+        start_wd=0.0,
+        end_wd=0.1,
+        wd_incr_steps=1000,
+        wd_incr_style='linear',
+    )
+
+    state_dict = {
+        'max_lr': 0.2,
+        'min_lr': 0.0005,
+        'lr_warmup_steps': 200,
+        'lr_decay_steps': 2000,
+        'lr_decay_style': 'cosine',
+        'num_steps': 500,
+        'start_wd': 0.01,
+        'end_wd': 0.2,
+        'wd_incr_steps': 500,
+        'wd_incr_style': 'cosine',
+    }
+
+    scheduler.load_state_dict(state_dict)
+    param_group = mock_optimizer.param_groups[0]
+
+    # 500 steps into a 500 step ramp from 0.01 to 0.2 is exactly end_wd. The constructor
+    # schedule would give 0.05 at the same step, which is what the param group used to hold.
+    assert scheduler.get_wd() == pytest.approx(0.2)
+    assert param_group['weight_decay'] == pytest.approx(scheduler.get_wd())
+    assert param_group['lr'] == pytest.approx(scheduler.get_lr(param_group))
+
+
 # ── get_canonical_lr_for_logging tests ──────────────────────────────────────
 #
 # Returns the lr of the first default_config=True param group.  In practice
